extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community: investigators, institutional research administrators, and applicants for NIH funding
extracted.subtask_description: A news/update page summarizing recent NIH extramural policy, program, and process changes relevant to people who apply for or administer NIH grants. Contains pointers to new formats, initiatives, and review-process modifications applicants should note.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of research models (New Approach Methodologies - NAMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: "NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches to advance our understanding of human health and disease. As we continue to encourage approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential, investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing studies/applications, choose the model systems best matched to the scientific question; consider NAMs for human relevance and translational potential but ensure scientific appropriateness rather than selecting a model solely to align with NIH priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: PF5 Collaborative International Research Projects: application format and linked awards
rubrics_metrics.description: "New Video Overview for NIH’s Collaborative International Research Projects (PF5) ... learn key features, application format, and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the PF5 application format and instructions; be aware that multi-component or collaborative applications may be administratively split into linked awards after review—plan budgets, aims, and coordination accordingly. Review the NIH overview/video for specific formatting and structural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: "We have issued a new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plans."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the 2026 Pilot DMS Plan template/format and include the required elements specified by NIH. Ensure DMS plans conform to the simplified required elements rather than older or ad hoc formats; consult the issued format for exact content and length expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replication and reproducibility expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: "Embedding Replication and Reproducibility Throughout NIH Research: Key Reminders for Applications, Awards, and a New Highlighted Topic ... NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan advances this commitment ... launched a new Replication and Reproducibility Initiative."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address replication and reproducibility in applications where relevant (study design, statistical power, replication plans, data sharing, methods transparency). Align proposals with NIH's emphasis on reproducibility and consider including explicit replication aims or plans to enhance robustness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring/process designation: 'Competitive But Not Discussed' (middle third / 33% cutoff)
rubrics_metrics.description: "...strong applications may fall below a 33% cut off, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as 'competitive but not discussed.'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that, per recent review modifications, applications falling into the middle third of the study section ranking may be labeled 'competitive but not discussed'—this affects whether applications are discussed at the meeting and has implications for resubmission strategy and interpretation of priority scores. Familiarize yourself with current CSR review policies and any temporary or emergency modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralization of NIH peer review within CSR
rubrics_metrics.description: "In March 2025, NIH announced that all peer review would be centralized within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR) ... update on the consolidation and its initial effects on the peer-review process."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that peer review processes, assignment, and possibly study section composition/procedures may change under centralization—monitor CSR guidance for impacts on submission routing, review timing, and reviewer expectations and adjust application strategies accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Small Business Program (Seed Fund) reactivation
rubrics_metrics.description: "It’s Official: NIH’s Small Business Program Is Back ... NIH’s Seed Fund is back in action!"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small business applicants and entrepreneurs should watch for reopenings of solicitations, program timelines, eligibility criteria, and application instructions associated with the reactivated Seed Fund and Small Business Program.
